title: Dense Pumpernickel Rye Loaf with Caraway
summary: A dense, dark rye loaf flavoured with caraway and a hint of cocoa, with a close, moist crumb suited to thin slicing.
equipment: large bowl or stand mixer with dough hook

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
dark rye flour, plus extra for dusting

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Boil 230 ml of the water, whisk in 70 g cornmeal and stir over low heat until thick, 1-2 min.

steps.title: Flavour
steps.text: Off the heat stir in 85 g treacle, 15 g butter, 1½ tsp salt, 2 tsp sugar, 2 tsp caraway seeds and 1 tbsp cocoa, then cool to lukewarm.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the remaining 110 ml cold water, 2½ tsp yeast, 320 g rye flour, 115 g wholemeal flour and 170 g mashed potato, then knead to a stiff, sticky dough for about 5 min.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Press the dough into a greased loaf tin and smooth the top.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Cover and leave until risen just to the rim of the tin, 60-90 min.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Dust with rye flour, score lightly and bake at 190 °C until the centre reaches 93 °C, 55-65 min.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Turn out onto a rack and cool completely, ideally several hours, before slicing thinly.

tips: Tent the loaf with foil if it starts to darken too quickly during the long bake.
Check the centre reaches 93 °C with a thermometer rather than judging by colour alone.
Let the loaf cool completely, ideally for several hours, before slicing so it holds together.
storage: Keeps well wrapped at room temperature for several days; slice thinly as needed and toast to refresh. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
